# Notes CLI — Design Decisions & Schema

## Project Layout

```
/
├── notes_cli/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── main.py      # Click entry point
│   ├── schema.py    # Dataclass + validation
│   └── storage.py   # JSON file I/O, ID management
├── notes_data/      # One JSON file per note: <id>.json
├── notes/
│   └── plan.md      # This file
└── pyproject.toml
```

## Note Schema

| Field      | Type            | Required | Notes                                      |
|------------|-----------------|----------|--------------------------------------------|
| `id`       | `int`           | auto     | Auto-incremented from 1; derived from max existing ID |
| `title`    | `str`           | yes      | Non-empty string                           |
| `tags`     | `list[str]`     | yes      | Empty list `[]` is valid; comma-separated on CLI |
| `body`     | `str`           | yes      | Multi-line content allowed                 |
| `citation` | `str \| None`   | no       | BibTeX entry string (not validated for format) |

JSON file per note stored as `notes_data/<id>.json`.

## ID Strategy

On `add`, the storage layer scans all `*.json` files in `notes_data/`, extracts IDs, and assigns `max(ids) + 1` (or `1` if empty). This avoids a separate counter file and is safe for manual edits/deletions.

## CLI Design

```
notes add --title TEXT --body TEXT [--tags TAG]... [--citation TEXT]
notes ls
notes show <id>
notes rm <id>
notes search <query>
```

- `--tags` is repeatable (e.g. `--tags python --tags research`) for clean shell UX.
- All required flags raise a `UsageError` if missing rather than prompting interactively.
- Output on success: a one-line confirmation with the assigned ID.
- `ls` — lists all notes as `<id>\t<title>` lines.
- `show <id>` — prints all fields of one note; exits with error if not found.
- `rm <id>` — deletes the note's JSON file; exits with error if not found.
- `search <query>` — case-insensitive substring match against title and body; lists matching notes as `<id>\t<title>`.

## Storage Format

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "title": "My Note",
  "tags": ["python", "cli"],
  "body": "Full body text here.",
  "citation": null
}
```

Files are pretty-printed (indent=2) for readability/git-diff friendliness.

## Extensibility Hooks

- `schema.py` uses `dataclasses` so future fields are easy to add.
- `storage.py` exposes `save_note`, `load_note`, `list_notes` — ready for `list`, `show`, `delete` commands.

4. `rm` — delete a note by ID

Everything works. Here's a summary of what was built:

---

**Files created:**

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` | Makes the package pip-installable; registers `notes` entry point |
| `notes_cli/main.py` | Click CLI — `notes add` command |
| `notes_cli/schema.py` | `Note` dataclass with `to_dict` / `from_dict` |
| `notes_cli/storage.py` | JSON file I/O, auto-incrementing ID logic |
| `notes/plan.md` | Design decisions and schema reference |

**Key design decisions:**

- **One file per note** (`notes_data/<id>.json`) — easy to inspect, delete, or version-control individual notes.
- **ID auto-increment** — scans existing filenames for `max(id) + 1`; no counter file needed, survives manual deletes.
- **`--tags` is repeatable** (`--tags ml --tags nlp`) — cleaner than comma-parsing in shell.
- **`citation` stored as raw string** — BibTeX is accepted as-is; format validation can be layered in later.

**Usage:**
```bash
pip install -e .

notes add --title "My Note" --body "Body text" --tags python --tags cli
notes add --title "Paper" --body "..." --tags ml --citation "@article{...}"
```

# Notes CLI — Design Decisions & Schema

## Project Layout

```
/
├── notes_cli/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── main.py      # Click entry point
│   ├── schema.py    # Dataclass + validation
│   └── storage.py   # JSON file I/O, ID management
├── notes_data/      # One JSON file per note: <id>.json
├── notes/
│   └── plan.md      # This file
└── pyproject.toml
```

## Note Schema

| Field      | Type            | Required | Notes                                      |
|------------|-----------------|----------|--------------------------------------------|
| `id`       | `int`           | auto     | Auto-incremented from 1; derived from max existing ID |
| `title`    | `str`           | yes      | Non-empty string                           |
| `tags`     | `list[str]`     | yes      | Empty list `[]` is valid; comma-separated on CLI |
| `body`     | `str`           | yes      | Multi-line content allowed                 |
| `citation` | `str \| None`   | no       | BibTeX entry string (not validated for format) |

JSON file per note stored as `notes_data/<id>.json`.

## ID Strategy

On `add`, the storage layer scans all `*.json` files in `notes_data/`, extracts IDs, and assigns `max(ids) + 1` (or `1` if empty). This avoids a separate counter file and is safe for manual edits/deletions.

## CLI Design

```
notes add --title TEXT --body TEXT [--tags TAG]... [--citation TEXT]
```

- `--tags` is repeatable (e.g. `--tags python --tags research`) for clean shell UX.
- All required flags raise a `UsageError` if missing rather than prompting interactively.
- Output on success: a one-line confirmation with the assigned ID.

## Storage Format

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "title": "My Note",
  "tags": ["python", "cli"],
  "body": "Full body text here.",
  "citation": null
}
```

Files are pretty-printed (indent=2) for readability/git-diff friendliness.

## Extensibility Hooks

- `schema.py` uses `dataclasses` so future fields are easy to add.
- `storage.py` exposes `save_note`, `load_note`, `list_notes` — ready for `list`, `show`, `delete` commands.
